main.description: A chunk of timed captions for a livestream or video. Word timing uses the compact encoding of tv.ionosphere.transcript: the words of `text` (split on whitespace) pair in order with the positive entries of `timings`, each a word duration in milliseconds, and each word starts where the previous one ended. A negative entry is a silence gap (absolute value, in milliseconds) before the next word. Long transcripts are split across several records.

subject.description: The place.stream.livestream or place.stream.video these captions belong to.

mediaStart.description: For livestream subjects: the wall-clock instant (millisecond precision) that `startMs` is measured from, which is the start time of the live session's first segment. Every chunk of a live session repeats the same value. Absent for video subjects, whose offsets are measured from the start of the video.

startMs.description: Start of the first word, in milliseconds from the subject's media start.

text.description: Caption text. Word boundaries come from whitespace tokenization.

timings.description: Flat timing array: a positive entry is a word duration in milliseconds, and the Nth positive entry corresponds to the Nth whitespace token of `text`; a negative entry is a silence gap (absolute value, in milliseconds) before the next word.

language.description: BCP 47 language of the caption text.

kind.description: captions (the default when absent): the same language as the audio, for viewers who can't hear it. subtitles: a translation.

source.description: auto: speech recognition. ingest: supplied by the streamer at ingest (CEA-608/708 or pushCaptions). human: authored or corrected by a person. imported: converted from an uploaded caption file.

track.description: The place.stream.media.track text track this chunk mirrors, when the captions were mastered into the canonical stream.

node.description: DID of the node that generated the captions.
